ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In a uniform magnetic field whose direction is perpendicular to the paper inward, there is a U-shaped metal guide rail. The plane of the guide rail is perpendicular to the magnetic field. Metal rod PQ is placed on the guide rail and forms a closed loop PQRS with the guide rail. A circular metal wire frame T is located inside the region enclosed by the loop, and the wire frame is coplanar with the guide rail. Now let metal rod PQ suddenly move to the right. At the instant when the motion begins, regarding the direction of induced current, which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: In PQRS it is along the counterclockwise direction, and in T it is along the clockwise direction

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the many crosses in the figure represent a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper inward; the U-shaped metal guide rail and metal rod PQ form a closed loop PQRS, with PQ on the right side; the arrow shows metal rod PQ suddenly moving to the right; the circular metal wire frame T is located inside the region enclosed by the PQRS loop and is coplanar with the guide rail. Then reason: PQ moving to the right makes the area of the outer loop PQRS increase, so the inward magnetic flux through PQRS increases. According to Lenz's law, the induced current in PQRS must produce a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper outward to hinder this increase, so the induced current in PQRS is counterclockwise. This counterclockwise current produces a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper outward inside the loop, that is, at the location of circular ring T. At the instant when the motion just begins, the induced current in PQRS starts increasing from zero, so the outward magnetic flux through T increases. To hinder the increase of outward magnetic flux, circular ring T should produce a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper inward. By the right-hand rule, the direction of the circular current that produces an inward magnetic field is clockwise.
